COMPLETED (re-emitted with corrected artifact packaging — no analysis changes). All twelve required deliverables exist in the working directory and are now listed under their exact native relative output paths in the artifacts dictionary.

FINAL SUMMARY OF THE COMPLETED WORK:
1. Data discovery: the 1164 scattered (t,x,y,u) observations form a piecewise-constant field with three time-invariant plateaus at -1.2482, -0.5029, +0.2433 (jumps 0.745/0.746, robust noise sigma = 0.0496, coverage 0.676 of 32x32 spatial cells, ~35.7 pts/unit^2, near-uniform temporal distribution).
2. Dense reconstruction (reconstructed_field.npy, float32 [6,128,128], [t,y,x] with indexing="xy"): Gaussian-kernel weighted vote over the discovered plateau levels at each of the 6 evaluation timestamps (H=0.40 spatial, HT=0.08 temporal, truncated kernels normalized by retained mass; scattered data used as scattered points, no zero-filling). Plateaus stay exact; edges soften only over ~H.
3. Transition curves: exactly 2 straight curves at every timestamp (never forced). Fitted directly on the raw observations as moving lines s = c0 + v*t + b*w (s=(x+y)/sqrt2, w=(x-y)/sqrt2) by exact prefix-sum least squares: curve A (+u side = bulk): c0=+1.9859, v=-1.7500, b=+0.0320, rms 0.0499; curve B (+u side = high): c0=-1.5061, v=-0.2800, b=+0.0280, rms 0.0472 — both equal to the noise level. Quadratic-in-time and curvature terms do not reduce the SSE (straight lines, linear motion).
4. Geometry deliverables (transition_curves.npz / transition_normals.npz / transition_speeds.npz, keys t_0..t_5, [176,2]/[176,2]/[176] float32, (x,y) order, rows grouped per curve in per_curve order 88+88): points sampled on the fitted lines clipped to the domain; unit normals oriented toward increasing u (verified on the reconstruction on both sides); signed normal speeds v_n = -v/sqrt(1+b^2): +1.7491 (curve A) and +0.2799 (curve B) — both fronts advance along +n (the low plateau expands, the high plateau shrinks), so u_t < 0 at each front.
5. Governing rule (governing_model.json): piecewise-constant level-set propagation — three time-invariant plateaus separated by two straight lines advancing at constant per-curve normal speeds; equivalently u_t = -v_n|grad u| at each front. Evidence: (a) forcing one common speed on both curves (what uniform advection requires, their normals coinciding) gives displacement-fit rms 0.1490 vs 0.0343 per-curve; (b) u_t-based family comparison at curve points (finite differences of independent reconstructions at tk±0.06): advection 0.5529, level-set 0.4622, relaxation 0.5052; (c) plateau drift within 2 standard errors rejects relaxation. alpha_x=-0.6945, alpha_y=-0.7396 = mean front velocity vector mean(v_n*n), convention documented; per-curve parameters, npz row layout, plateau drift check and an in-script synthetic validation (max |speed error| 0.110, max |position error| 0.029) are recorded in the JSON. fit_residual_rms = 0.0517.
6. Consistency (consistency_report.json): observed u minus moving-step-model u at all 261 raw observations within 0.30 of a fitted curve (signed offset q along the reported normal, both sides sampled consistently): median -0.0064, p90 0.0603, pass_fraction_20pct = 1.000 (threshold 0.2*jump = 0.149).
7. Supporting artifacts: exploration_summary.json (n_observations, u_range, noise_estimate, coverage_estimate, 24-bin value histogram); model_candidates.json (3 families with motivations); diagnostic_report.json (per t_k: median/p90 residual near curves, u_t residual statistics, fitted line positions); transition_mask_preview.npy (bool [6,128,128], True fraction 0.062-0.070 within 2.5 cells of the curves); reconstruction_slices.png (valid 1282x846 PNG, 6 panels with curves and signed normal-speed arrows).

KNOWN LIMITATIONS: this environment lacks matplotlib (and network), so the delivered figure comes from the script's pure numpy+zlib fallback renderer (panels, curves, arrows, colorbar; no text annotations) — the script uses matplotlib automatically where available; the reconstruction shows ~0.4-unit edge softening and a slight temporal lag at t=0/t=T from the one-sided temporal kernel (documented in the methodology strings); the u_t target for family comparison is noise/edge-limited (median |residual| ~0.2) and was used only as supplementary evidence, with the raw-data displacement criterion as the sharper discriminator; the slow curve's speed carries ~0.1 absolute uncertainty per the synthetic validation, while positions are accurate to <=0.03.

Constraints honored throughout: numpy/scipy only (no ML libraries), single entry-point analysis.py with no arguments, scattered observations never reshaped into dense zero-filled tensors, runtime 14 s (well under 30 min), all shapes/dtypes/keys per the public submission contract.
